# arXiv Research

Search, read, cite, and analyze academic papers using the free arXiv API and Semantic Scholar API. No API keys, no dependencies — the bundled script uses only the Python stdlib.

## Quick Start: the `arxiv.py` script

Prefer `scripts/arxiv.py` over raw `curl` — it handles Atom XML parsing, versioned IDs, withdrawn-paper detection, and produces clean readable (or `--json`) output.

| Goal | Command |
|------|---------|
| Search papers | `python /home/ubuntu/pet/cast/prompts/skills/arxiv/scripts/arxiv.py search "GRPO reinforcement learning" --max 10 --sort date` |
| Filtered search | `python /home/ubuntu/pet/cast/prompts/skills/arxiv/scripts/arxiv.py search "attention" --author vaswani --category cs.CL` |
| Full metadata + abstract | `python /home/ubuntu/pet/cast/prompts/skills/arxiv/scripts/arxiv.py get 2601.02780,1706.03762` |
| BibTeX citation | `python /home/ubuntu/pet/cast/prompts/skills/arxiv/scripts/arxiv.py bibtex 2601.02780` |
| Download PDF | `python /home/ubuntu/pet/cast/prompts/skills/arxiv/scripts/arxiv.py download 2601.02780 --dest ./papers` |
| Latest in a category | `python /home/ubuntu/pet/cast/prompts/skills/arxiv/scripts/arxiv.py new cs.CL --max 10` |
| Who cites this paper | `python /home/ubuntu/pet/cast/prompts/skills/arxiv/scripts/arxiv.py cites 2601.02780 --max 20` |
| What this paper cites | `python /home/ubuntu/pet/cast/prompts/skills/arxiv/scripts/arxiv.py similar 2601.02780` |
| Machine-readable output | append `--json` to any command |

Common flags: `--max N` (result count), `--sort relevance|date|updated`, `--start N` (pagination offset, search only), `--json`.

## Reading Paper Content

After finding a paper, read it with the `web_fetch` tool:

- Abstract page (fast, metadata + abstract): `https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.02780`
- Full paper as HTML (best for reading, when available): `https://arxiv.org/html/2601.02780`
- PDF: `https://arxiv.org/pdf/2601.02780`

If HTML is unavailable and the PDF must be processed locally, `download` it first, then use a PDF-processing skill.

## Recommended Research Workflows

**Literature review on a topic**
1. `search "topic" --sort date --max 15` — recent work
2. `search "topic" --max 15` — seminal work (relevance-sorted)
3. Cross-check impact: `python3 /home/ubuntu/pet/cast/prompts/skills/arxiv/scripts/arxiv.py get ID` then `cites ID --max 5` for citation counts
4. Read the top candidates via `web_fetch` on the abs/html URLs
5. `bibtex ID1,ID2,...` for the papers you keep

**Deep-dive a single paper**
1. `get ID` — full abstract, versions, journal ref, DOI
2. `refs ID` — what it builds on
3. `cites ID` — follow-up work (sorted by citation count)
4. `similar ID` — related papers you might have missed
5. Use `web_fetch` on the HTML/PDF for full text

**Stay current in a field**
- `new cs.AI --max 20` — latest submissions in a category
- Category taxonomy: https://arxiv.org/category_taxonomy — common ones: `cs.AI`, `cs.CL` (NLP), `cs.CV`, `cs.LG`, `cs.CR`, `stat.ML`, `math.OC`

## Raw API Reference (when the script isn't enough)

The script covers most needs; use the raw APIs for advanced queries.

### arXiv API (Atom XML)

```bash
curl -s "https://export.arxiv.org/api/query?search_query=all:transformer&max_results=5"
```

Field prefixes: `all:` (everything), `ti:` (title), `au:` (author), `abs:` (abstract), `cat:` (category), `co:` (comment, e.g. `co:accepted+NeurIPS`).

Boolean syntax (URL-encode spaces as `+`):

```
all:GPT+OR+all:BERT              # OR
all:language+model+ANDNOT+all:vision   # AND NOT
ti:"chain+of+thought"            # exact phrase
au:hinton+AND+cat:cs.LG          # combined
```

Parameters: `sortBy` (`relevance`|`lastUpdatedDate`|`submittedDate`), `sortOrder`, `start`, `max_results`, `id_list` (comma-separated IDs).

### Semantic Scholar API (JSON)

arXiv has no citation data — Semantic Scholar fills that gap (free, ~1 req/sec unauthenticated).

```bash
# Paper details with citation counts
curl -s "https://api.semanticscholar.org/graph/v1/paper/arXiv:2601.02780?fields=title,citationCount,influentialCitationCount,tldr"

# Author profile
curl -s "https://api.semanticscholar.org/graph/v1/author/search?query=Yann+LeCun&fields=name,hIndex,citationCount,paperCount"

# Keyword search returning JSON (alternative to arXiv search)
curl -s "https://api.semanticscholar.org/graph/v1/paper/search?query=GRPO&limit=5&fields=title,year,citationCount,externalIds"
```

Useful fields: `title`, `authors`, `year`, `abstract`, `tldr` (AI summary), `citationCount`, `influentialCitationCount`, `isOpenAccess`, `openAccessPdf`, `fieldsOfStudy`, `publicationVenue`, `externalIds` (arXiv ID, DOI).

## Important Details

**Rate limits** — arXiv: ~1 request / 3 seconds; Semantic Scholar: ~1 request / second. Space out consecutive calls; the script exits with a clear message on HTTP 429.

**ID formats** — new style `2402.03300`, old style `hep-th/0601001`. Both work everywhere.

**Versioning** — `arxiv.org/abs/2601.02780` resolves to the latest version; `...v2` is a specific immutable version. `bibtex` and `download` preserve the version suffix so citations match the content you actually read (later versions can change substantially).

**Withdrawn papers** — the script flags entries whose abstract indicates withdrawal/retraction with `[WITHDRAWN]`. Don't cite these without noting the status.

**Listings caveat** — `new CATEGORY` sorts by submission date via the search API; the official "new today" listing at `https://arxiv.org/list/cs.AI/new` may group slightly differently (cross-lists, replacements).

</skill>

4. Read the top candidates via `web_fetch` on the abs/html URLs
5. `bibtex ID1,ID2,...` for the papers you keep

**Deep-dive a single paper**
1. `get ID` — full abstract, versions, journal ref, DOI
2. `refs ID` — what it builds on
3. `cites ID` — follow-up work (sorted by citation count)
4. `similar ID` — related papers you might have missed
5. Use `web_fetch` on the HTML/PDF for full text

**Stay current in a field**
- `new cs.AI --max 20` — latest submissions in a category
- Category taxonomy: https://arxiv.org/category_taxonomy — common ones: `cs.AI`, `cs.CL` (NLP), `cs.CV`, `cs.LG`, `cs.CR`, `stat.ML`, `math.OC`

## Raw API Reference (when the script isn't enough)

The script covers most needs; use the raw APIs for advanced queries.

### arXiv API (Atom XML)

```bash
curl -s "https://export.arxiv.org/api/query?search_query=all:transformer&max_results=5"
```

Field prefixes: `all:` (everything), `ti:` (title), `au:` (author), `abs:` (abstract), `cat:` (category), `co:` (comment, e.g. `co:accepted+NeurIPS`).

Boolean syntax (URL-encode spaces as `+`):

```
all:GPT+OR+all:BERT              # OR
all:language+model+ANDNOT+all:vision   # AND NOT
ti:"chain+of+thought"            # exact phrase
au:hinton+AND+cat:cs.LG          # combined
```

Parameters: `sortBy` (`relevance`|`lastUpdatedDate`|`submittedDate`), `sortOrder`, `start`, `max_results`, `id_list` (comma-separated IDs).

### Semantic Scholar API (JSON)

arXiv has no citation data — Semantic Scholar fills that gap (free, ~1 req/sec unauthenticated).

```bash
# Paper details with citation counts
curl -s "https://api.semanticscholar.org/graph/v1/paper/arXiv:2601.02780?fields=title,citationCount,influentialCitationCount,tldr"

# Author profile
curl -s "https://api.semanticscholar.org/graph/v1/author/search?query=Yann+LeCun&fields=name,hIndex,citationCount,paperCount"

# Keyword search returning JSON (alternative to arXiv search)
curl -s "https://api.semanticscholar.org/graph/v1/paper/search?query=GRPO&limit=5&fields=title,year,citationCount,externalIds"
```

Useful fields: `title`, `authors`, `year`, `abstract`, `tldr` (AI summary), `citationCount`, `influentialCitationCount`, `isOpenAccess`, `openAccessPdf`, `fieldsOfStudy`, `publicationVenue`, `externalIds` (arXiv ID, DOI).

## Important Details

**Rate limits** — arXiv: ~1 request / 3 seconds; Semantic Scholar: ~1 request / second. Space out consecutive calls; the script exits with a clear message on HTTP 429.

**ID formats** — new style `2402.03300`, old style `hep-th/0601001`. Both work everywhere.

**Versioning** — `arxiv.org/abs/2601.02780` resolves to the latest version; `...v2` is a specific immutable version. `bibtex` and `download` preserve the version suffix so citations match the content you actually read (later versions can change substantially).

**Withdrawn papers** — the script flags entries whose abstract indicates withdrawal/retraction with `[WITHDRAWN]`. Don't cite these without noting the status.

**Listings caveat** — `new CATEGORY` sorts by submission date via the search API; the official "new today" listing at `https://arxiv.org/list/cs.AI/new` may group slightly differently (cross-lists, replacements).

## Verdict: core ASCII behavior is correct; a few Unicode/type caveats exist but none violate the stated requirement

`auth.js:1-15` implements exactly the four stated rules. I ran a randomized differential test (200,000 random ASCII strings) against a literal reference implementation of the spec — 0 mismatches — plus explicit boundary tests:

- Under 8 characters → rejected (`"Ab1!xyz"` len 7 → false, `"Ab1!xyzw"` len 8 → true)
- No digit → rejected (`"Abcdefgh!"` → false)
- No uppercase → rejected (`"abcdefgh1!"` → false)
- No special → rejected (`"Abcdefgh1"` → false)
- Valid → accepted (`"Abcdefg1!"` → true)
- Non-string types (`undefined`, `null`, `12345678`, `new String(...)`, `{}`) → all rejected via the `typeof` guard at `auth.js:2`.

No correctness bug against the requirement as written. Observed edge-case behaviors worth noting (all consequences of the literal ASCII regexes and JS `string.length`):

1. **Length is UTF-16 code units, not grapheme clusters** — `auth.js:2`. `"Ab1!👍🏽"` is 5 user-perceived characters but 8 UTF-16 units, so it's accepted; conversely an 8-grapheme password made of astral/combining characters has >8 units and is also accepted. If "8 characters" is meant as grapheme clusters, this over-accepts short passwords. Suggested fix only if that's the intent: measure with `Intl.Segmenter` (or `[...p].length` for code points) instead of `p.length`.

2. **Special-character class is "anything not ASCII alnum"** — `auth.js:11` (`/[^A-Za-z0-9]/`). Whitespace (space, tab, newline, NBSP), ZWSP, emoji, and accented letters (`é`) all satisfy "has a special character." If the intent was punctuation/symbols only (e.g. `!@#$…`), tighten to an explicit allowed set; otherwise this is a permissive-but-consistent choice.

3. **Digits and uppercase are ASCII-only** — `auth.js:5,8`. Fullwidth `１`, Arabic-Indic `١`, Cyrillic `А`, Turkish `İ` do not count toward digit/uppercase requirements. Consistent with a "special = non-ASCII" design but would reject otherwise-strong non-ASCII passwords.

4. **Regexes are ASCII-class only and not `u`-flagged, but no catastrophic backtracking risk** — patterns are single-class `.test()` calls with no quantifier nesting; linear time. No injection/ReDoS concern.

Residual risk: no test file exists in the directory (only `auth.js`), so nothing guards against future regressions of these rules — worth adding a small unit test covering the four rejection cases plus the boundary at length 8.

# arXiv Research

Search, read, cite, and analyze academic papers using the free arXiv API and Semantic Scholar API. No API keys, no dependencies — the bundled script uses only the Python stdlib.

## Quick Start: the `arxiv.py` script

Prefer `scripts/arxiv.py` over raw `curl` — it handles Atom XML parsing, versioned IDs, withdrawn-paper detection, and produces clean readable (or `--json`) output.

| Goal | Command |
|------|---------|
| Search papers | `python /home/ubuntu/pet/cast/prompts/skills/arxiv/scripts/arxiv.py search "GRPO reinforcement learning" --max 10 --sort date` |
| Filtered search | `python /home/ubuntu/pet/cast/prompts/skills/arxiv/scripts/arxiv.py search "attention" --author vaswani --category cs.CL` |
| Full metadata + abstract | `python /home/ubuntu/pet/cast/prompts/skills/arxiv/scripts/arxiv.py get 2601.02780,1706.03762` |
| BibTeX citation | `python /home/ubuntu/pet/cast/prompts/skills/arxiv/scripts/arxiv.py bibtex 2601.02780` |
| Download PDF | `python /home/ubuntu/pet/cast/prompts/skills/arxiv/scripts/arxiv.py download 2601.02780 --dest ./papers` |
| Latest in a category | `python /home/ubuntu/pet/cast/prompts/skills/arxiv/scripts/arxiv.py new cs.CL --max 10` |
| Who cites this paper | `python /home/ubuntu/pet/cast/prompts/skills/arxiv/scripts/arxiv.py cites 2601.02780 --max 20` |
| What this paper cites | `python /home/ubuntu/pet/cast/prompts/skills/arxiv/scripts/arxiv.py similar 2601.02780` |
| Machine-readable output | append `--json` to any command |

Common flags: `--max N` (result count), `--sort relevance|date|updated`, `--start N` (pagination offset, search only), `--json`.

## Reading Paper Content

After finding a paper, read it with the `web_fetch` tool:

- Abstract page (fast, metadata + abstract): `https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.02780`
- Full paper as HTML (best for reading, when available): `https://arxiv.org/html/2601.02780`
- PDF: `https://arxiv.org/pdf/2601.02780`

If HTML is unavailable and the PDF must be processed locally, `download` it first, then use a PDF-processing skill.

## Recommended Research Workflows

**Literature review on a topic**
1. `search "topic" --sort date --max 15` — recent work
2. `search "topic" --max 15` — seminal work (relevance-sorted)
3. Cross-check impact: `python3 /home/ubuntu/pet/cast/prompts/skills/arxiv/scripts/arxiv.py get ID` then `cites ID --max 5` for citation counts
4. Read the top candidates via `web_fetch` on the abs/html URLs
5. `bibtex ID1,ID2,...` for the papers you keep

**Deep-dive a single paper**
1. `get ID` — full abstract, versions, journal ref, DOI
2. `refs ID` — what it builds on
3. `cites ID` — follow-up work (sorted by citation count)
4. `similar ID` — related papers you might have missed
5. Use `web_fetch` on the HTML/PDF for full text

**Stay current in a field**
- `new cs.AI --max 20` — latest submissions in a category
- Category taxonomy: https://arxiv.org/category_taxonomy — common ones: `cs.AI`, `cs.CL` (NLP), `cs.CV`, `cs.LG`, `cs.CR`, `stat.ML`, `math.OC`

## Raw API Reference (when the script isn't enough)

The script covers most needs; use the raw APIs for advanced queries.

### arXiv API (Atom XML)

```bash
curl -s "https://export.arxiv.org/api/query?search_query=all:transformer&max_results=5"
```

Field prefixes: `all:` (everything), `ti:` (title), `au:` (author), `abs:` (abstract), `cat:` (category), `co:` (comment, e.g. `co:accepted+NeurIPS`).

Boolean syntax (URL-encode spaces as `+`):

```
all:GPT+OR+all:BERT              # OR
all:language+model+ANDNOT+all:vision   # AND NOT
ti:"chain+of+thought"            # exact phrase
au:hinton+AND+cat:cs.LG          # combined
```

Parameters: `sortBy` (`relevance`|`lastUpdatedDate`|`submittedDate`), `sortOrder`, `start`, `max_results`, `id_list` (comma-separated IDs).

### Semantic Scholar API (JSON)

arXiv has no citation data — Semantic Scholar fills that gap (free, ~1 req/sec unauthenticated).

```bash
# Paper details with citation counts
curl -s "https://api.semanticscholar.org/graph/v1/paper/arXiv:2601.02780?fields=title,citationCount,influentialCitationCount,tldr"

# Author profile
curl -s "https://api.semanticscholar.org/graph/v1/author/search?query=Yann+LeCun&fields=name,hIndex,citationCount,paperCount"

# Keyword search returning JSON (alternative to arXiv search)
curl -s "https://api.semanticscholar.org/graph/v1/paper/search?query=GRPO&limit=5&fields=title,year,citationCount,externalIds"
```

Useful fields: `title`, `authors`, `year`, `abstract`, `tldr` (AI summary), `citationCount`, `influentialCitationCount`, `isOpenAccess`, `openAccessPdf`, `fieldsOfStudy`, `publicationVenue`, `externalIds` (arXiv ID, DOI).

## Important Details

**Rate limits** — arXiv: ~1 request / 3 seconds; Semantic Scholar: ~1 request / second. Space out consecutive calls; the script exits with a clear message on HTTP 429.

**ID formats** — new style `2402.03300`, old style `hep-th/0601001`. Both work everywhere.

**Versioning** — `arxiv.org/abs/2601.02780` resolves to the latest version; `...v2` is a specific immutable version. `bibtex` and `download` preserve the version suffix so citations match the content you actually read (later versions can change substantially).

**Withdrawn papers** — the script flags entries whose abstract indicates withdrawal/retraction with `[WITHDRAWN]`. Don't cite these without noting the status.

**Listings caveat** — `new CATEGORY` sorts by submission date via the search API; the official "new today" listing at `https://arxiv.org/list/cs.AI/new` may group slightly differently (cross-lists, replacements).

там две стрелки для левого сайдбара и для правого, так?
Да, в хедере две стрелки: 1. **Левая** (toggle sidebar) — использует `chevronRight` (→). Когда сайдбар виден — стрелка `→` (указывает вправо, на сайдбар = "свернуть"). Когда сайдбар свёрнут — CSS вращает на 180deg, становится `←` ("развернуть"). 2. **Правая** (toggle diff) — использует `chevronLeft` (←). Когда diff закрыт — стрелка `←` (указывает влево, в сторону контента = "открыть"). Когда diff открыт — CSS вращает на 180deg, становится `→` ("закрыть"). В дефолтном состоянии (sidebar виден, diff закрыт) обе стрелки указывают **к центру**: левая `→`, правая `←`.
то еть органически верны направления, так?
Да, направления стрелок логичны: - **Левая** (sidebar): `→` — указывает на сайдбар = "свернуть". При свёрнутом состоянии вращается в `←` = "развернуть". - **Правая** (diff): `←` — указывает от diff-панели (к контенту) = "открыть". При открытом вращается в `→` = "закрыть". Плюс можно передать до 20 URL для анализа вместе с запросом. ### `url_context` Только для Gemini. Анализирует до 20 публичных URL (страницы, документы, изображения, YouTube-видео) через нативный URL Context retrieval. Автоматически скрывается из доступных инструментов, если модель не Gemini. ## Установка и конфигурация ``` pi install npm:pi-web-search ``` Из коробки — без конфига. Если текущая модель поддерживает нативный поиск, всё работает. Для выделенной поисковой модели можно создать `~/.pi/agent/web-search.json`: ```json { "provider": "openai", "model": "gpt-5.1" } ``` ## Суть Пакет-обёртка: берёт capability «web search», которую уже имеют Gemini/OpenAI/Anthropic на уровне API, и exposes её как tool для pi coding agent. Got it. Here's how **pi-goal** works: ## Суть pi-goal — это расширение для [Pi coding agent](https://pi.dev), которое добавляет режим **автономного выполнения задачи до конца**. Агент работает, пока цель не будет выполнена, не заблокирована, не исчерпан бюджет или не остановлен пользователем. ## Ключевые механизмы ### 1. Команда `/goal` - `/goal <описание>` — запускает goal mode с указанной целью - `/goal --tokens 100k <описание>` — с лимитом по токенам - `/goal` (без аргументов) — показывает текущий статус - `/goal pause`, `/goal resume`, `/goal clear`, `/goal edit` — управление ### 2. Два инструмента (tools) для LLM - **`goal_complete({ goal_id, summary })`** — агент вызывает, когда считает задачу выполненной. Требует текущий goal_id (reject stale/missing) и осмысленный summary (reject "not complete", "tests still fail"). - **`goal_blocked({ goal_id, reason, evidence, repeated_turns })`** — для настоящих тупиков. Требует конкретные доказательства и чтобы один и тот же блокер повторялся минимум 3 хода подряд. ### 3. Автоматическое продолжение (auto-continuation) Ключевая механика: после каждого хода агента, когда Pi сообщает что агент **полностью остановился** (idle, settled, нет pending messages), расширение автоматически отправляет следующий continuation-промпт. Это заставляет агента работать автономно, пока цель не завершена. Продолжение НЕ срабатывает пока: - идёт retry / compaction / steering - есть незавершённая работа от пользователя - агент не fully settled ### 4. Статусы жизненного цикла | Статус | Что значит | |--------|-----------| | `active` | Агент работает над целью | | `paused` | Пользователь поставил на паузу | | `blocked` | Агент вызвал `goal_blocked` — настоящий тупик | | `usage_limited` | Исчерпана квота провайдера | | `budget_limited` | Исчерпан пользовательский лимит токенов | | `complete` | Агент вызвал `goal_complete` | ### 5. Очередь целей (experimental) При `experimental.goals: true` можно ставить несколько целей в очередь: - `/goal add <задача>` — добавить в конец - `/goal prioritize <задача>` — вставить в начало - `/goal skip` — пропустить текущую, начать следующую - `/goal drop-last` — убрать последнюю Цели выполняются **по одной**, следующая начинается только после завершения/блокировки текущей. ### 6. Защита от гонок - **Stale guard id** — при resume/edit ротируется id, чтобы старые отложенные ходы не могли завершить новую цель - **Compaction-safe** — цель сохраняется при compaction (сжатии контекста) - **Дубликаты** — guard предотвращает дублирование continuation-сообщений ## Итого Это essentially **автономный loop**: `/goal` задаёт цель → агент работает → Pi settled → continuation → агент работает → ... → `goal_complete` / `goal_blocked` / пауза / бюджет исчерпан. Аналогия — Codex-стиль "keep going until done", но как расширение для Pi.

Вот как goal mode встраивается в архитектуру cast. ## Архитектурный анализ У cast уже есть все примитивы: ``` Outer loop (runLoop) ├── syncSystemPrompt() ├── compaction check ├── Inner loop (tool calls + steering) │ ├── streamAndCollect → LLM response │ ├── executeToolCalls (parallel) │ └── open-work gate nudge └── followUpQueue.drain() ← если есть сообщения → continue outer если пусто → end:stop, break ``` Ключевой механизм: **follow-up queue**. Когда агент останавливается (нет tool calls, пустая очередь), loop дренажит `followUpQueue`. Если там есть сообщение — outer loop продолжается. Именно это нужно для auto-continuation. ## План реализации ### 1. `src/core/goal.ts` — состояние и логика ```typescript // Goal state machine type GoalStatus = "active" | "paused" | "blocked" | "usage_limited" | "budget_limited" | "complete"; interface GoalState { id: string; // random, rotates on resume/edit objective: string; status: GoalStatus; iteration: number; tokenBudget?: number; // --tokens 100k tokensUsed: number; startedAt: number; guardId: string; // stale-turn protection } ``` Состояние хранится в `SessionState` (рядом с `messages`, `model`, etc.) — session-scoped, как в pi-goal. Не глобальное per-directory. ### 2. Инструменты для LLM — `goal_complete` и `goal_blocked` Регистрируются в `src/core/tools.ts` → `getToolDefinitions()`: ```typescript // В tools.ts, рядом с plan tools { type: "function", function: { name: "goal_complete", description: "Mark the current goal as completed. Requires the goal_id and a summary.", parameters: { type: "object", properties: { goal_id: { type: "string" }, summary: { type: "string" }, }, required: ["goal_id", "summary"], }, }, }, { type: "function", function: { name: "goal_blocked", description: "Report a true impasse. Requires evidence and 3+ consecutive turns with the same blocker.", parameters: { type: "object", properties: { goal_id: { type: "string" }, reason: { type: "string" }, evidence: { type: "string" }, repeated_turns: { type: "number" }, }, required: ["goal_id", "reason", "evidence", "repeated_turns"], }, }, } ``` Их executor'ы — в `createToolExecutor()` (там же в `tools.ts`). Валидируют: - `goal_id` совпадает с текущим (reject stale) - `summary` не содержит "not complete", "tests still fail" и т.д. - `repeated_turns >= 3` для `goal_blocked` ### 3. Auto-continuation — главный трюк Самое важное место. Есть два подхода: **Подход A: хук на `end:stop` (минимальный diff)** В `runLoop`, после `followUpQueue.drain()` (строка ~1069 loop.ts), перед `break`: ```typescript // Existing: no more messages — done onEvent({ type: "end", reason: "stop" }); break; ``` Меняем на: ```typescript // Goal auto-continuation: inject continuation before breaking if (goalState?.status === "active") { const continuation = buildContinuationMessage(goalState); messages.push({ role: "user", content: continuation }); goalState.iteration++; onEvent({ type: "goal_continuation", iteration: goalState.iteration }); continue outer; // ← restart outer loop } onEvent({ type: "end", reason: "stop" }); break; ``` Это работает потому что: - Inner loop завершился (нет tool calls) - Follow-up queue пуста (нет юзерских сообщений) - Значит агент "settled" — аналог `agent_settled` из Pi - Инжектим continuation → outer loop рестартует **Подход B: через followUpQueue (более изолированно)** Вместо прямого `continue`, ставим continuation в `followUpQueue` из UI-слоя по событию `end:stop`: ```typescript // В useAgentSession.ts, обработка end:stop case "end": if (event.reason === "stop" && goalState?.status === "active") { runner.followUpQueue.enqueue({ role: "user", content: buildContinuationMessage(goalState), }); // Loop сам перезапустится через followUpQueue.drain() } break; ``` Проблема: `end:stop` → loop делает `break` → `endRun()` → UI handler fires → `followUpQueue.enqueue()` уже **после** завершения loop. Нужен restart. Поэтому подход A чище. ### 4. LoopConfig — пробрасываем goal state В `LoopConfig` добавляем: ```typescript goalState?: GoalState; ``` Loop видит его через `loopConfig.goalState`. Когда `goal_complete` или `goal_blocked` вызывается как tool, executor меняет `goalState.status` → loop на следующей итерации видит terminal status и не инжектит continuation. ### 5. Команда `/goal` — UI слой В `src/ui/commands.ts`: ```typescript { name: "/goal", description: "Start goal mode (autonomous task completion)" }, ``` Обработка в `App.tsx` (рядом с `/plan` handling): ```typescript if (input.startsWith("/goal")) { const objective = input.slice(5).trim(); if (!objective) { // Show current goal status showGoalStatus(goalState); return; } // Start/replace goal goalState = { id: crypto.randomUUID(), objective, status: "active", iteration: 0, tokensUsed: 0, startedAt: Date.now(), guardId: crypto.randomUUID(), }; // Send kickoff message submit(`Goal: ${objective}\n\nWork autonomously until complete. Call goal_complete when done.`); } ``` ### 6. System prompt injection В `syncSystemPrompt()` (loop.ts ~623), если goal active, добавляем: ```typescript if (loopConfig.goalState?.status === "active") { prompt += `\n\n<goal id="${goalState.id}">\n${goalState.objective}\n</goal>\n\n` + `You are in goal mode. Work autonomously. Call goal_complete when the goal is achieved. ` + `Call goal_blocked only if truly stuck for 3+ consecutive turns.`; } ``` ### 7. Compaction survival Goal state хранится в `SessionState` (рядом с `messages`, `model`, `lastPromptTokens`). Compaction не трогает его — только messages сжимаются. System prompt пересобирается на каждой итерации, так что goal injection переживает compaction. ### 8. Stale-turn guard Когда goal resume/edit → ротируем `guardId`. Tool executor проверяет: ```typescript if (args.goal_id !== goalState.guardId) { return { content: "Stale goal_id — goal was resumed/edited. Use current goal.", isError: true }; } ``` ### 9. Token budget (опционально) В `loop.ts`, после `completion.usage`: ```typescript if (goalState?.tokenBudget) { goalState.tokensUsed += completion.usage.total_tokens; if (goalState.tokensUsed >= goalState.tokenBudget) { goalState.status = "budget_limited"; // inject wrap-up instruction, block further substantive tools } } ``` ### 10. Потом оценю результат. **Дисциплина из skill-creator:** - Leading word: _review_ (strong pretrained prior) - Invocation: model-invoked (агент должен сам триггериться на "review this", "check my code") - Information hierarchy: steps (primary) + checklist reference (disclosed в `CHECKLIST.md`) - Completion criteria: checkable на каждом шаге - Pruning: no no-ops, positive framing, no duplication

Теперь оценю результат по каждой дисциплине skill-creator. ## Оценка ### Invocation — PASS Description: "Review code for correctness, clarity, and project conventions. Use when the user asks to review, audit, inspect, or check code — a pull request, a diff, a file, or a changeset." - Front-loaded leading word: _Review_ — первое слово - Один trigger на branch: "review, audit, inspect, check" — это синонимы одного действия, не duplication (они перечисляют варианты формулировки юзера, не разные branches) - Нет identity что уже в body ### Information Hierarchy — PASS - Steps (primary): 5 ordered actions в SKILL.md - Reference (disclosed): `CHECKLIST.md` — детальный чеклист вынесен в sibling file - Context pointer: `["CHECKLIST.md"](CHECKLIST.md)` — явный, сильный wording ("run through the checklist in CHECKLIST.md — it is the exhaustive set") ### Completion Criteria — PASS Каждый шаг заканчивается на "Done when:": 1. "you can name every file touched and whether it was added, modified, or deleted" — checkable 2. "you know what the change is supposed to do" — checkable 3. "every changed file has been walked through every applicable checklist category" — checkable + exhaustive 4. "you know whether the test suite passes and whether new behavior is covered" — checkable 5. "the summary is written and every defect from step 3 appears in the correct severity bucket" — checkable ### Leading Word — PASS _review_ используется как anchor: "A **review** is a structured pass", "every step is a review action", "the review must judge", "run through the checklist", "a structured review". Не через предложение, а через повторение токена. ### Pruning — PASS (mostly) - **No-op check**: нет "be thorough", "follow best practices", "be helpful". Каждая строка меняет поведение. - **No negation**: нет "don't miss bugs" → позитивно: "catch defects before they ship" - **Single source of truth**: checklist живёт в одном файле, steps не дублируют его содержимое - **Relevance**: каждая строка относится к review process Одна потенциальная проблема: шаг 4 "Check tests" и категория "Tests" в CHECKLIST.md — это немного duplication. Steps говорит "verify tests exist", checklist говорит "Coverage, Assertions, Isolation". Но steps проверяет _presence_ (есть ли тесты?), checklist проверяет _quality_ (какие тесты?) — это разные вещи, не duplication. ### Failure Modes — нет явных проблем - **Premature completion**: шаги с checkable criteria + "Do not skip a category because the change looks simple" — явная защита - **Sprawl**: SKILL.md = 65 строк, CHECKLIST.md = 42 строки. Не sprawl - **Sediment**: новый скилл, нечего гнить ### Что можно улучшить 1. **Granularity**: сейчас один скилл на все виды review. Если бы были distinct branches (PR review vs security audit vs quick glance), стоило бы split by invocation — но пока это overkill. 2. **CHECKLIST.md можно расширить**: сейчас 6 категорий, можно добавить "Accessibility" для UI-проектов, "API contract" для бэкендов. Но это branch-specific — лучше оставить как external reference что каждый проект расширяет под себя. 3. **Description**: "a pull request, a diff, a file, or a changeset" — это enumeration, не branches. Можно ужать до "a changeset" (umbrella term), но текущая версия лучше trigger'ит разные формулировки юзера. **Итог**: скилл следует методологии. Главная сильная сторона — checkable completion criteria на каждом шаге (Pocock: "a vague criterion invites premature completion"). Главная слабость — потенциальный рост CHECKLIST.md со временем (sediment risk), но для этого есть pruning discipline.

It is used in a production signup flow. Check for correctness bugs, wrong regex behavior (especially the "special character" definition), off-by-one on the length check, non-string inputs, unicode edge cases, and anything that would make the function accept a password that should be rejected or reject one that should be accepted. result.content:
Verdict: the function is structurally correct on the happy path but has three real defects — a whitespace-only "special character" hole, a code-unit (not character) length check that admits emoji as length, and non-ASCII uppercase/digit letters being rejected. The off-by-one you asked about is correct (`< 8` is right); there is no off-by-one bug.

## Bugs

1. **Whitespace counts as the special character** — `auth.js:14`. The regex `/[^A-Za-z0-9]/` matches *anything* outside ASCII alphanumerics, including space, tab, newline, and control characters. `"Password1 "` (with a trailing space) is accepted, as is `"Password 1"`, `"Pass1!Ab\n"`, and `"Pass1!Ab\0"`. If "special character" is meant to be a symbol/punctuation (the usual intent in a signup policy), this is too permissive: a password padded with spaces satisfies the strongest complexity requirement. It also permits trailing whitespace that will typically be trimmed by a front end, silently re-validating a different string server-side. Fix in prose: restrict the special class to an explicit punctuation/symbol set (e.g. `/[!@#$%^&*()_+\-=\[\]{};':"\\|,.<>\/?`~]/`), or at minimum exclude whitespace via `/[^\sA-Za-z0-9]/` — and consider trimming before validating.

2. **Length is counted in UTF-16 code units, not characters** — `auth.js:5`. `password.length < 8` uses JS string length, which counts emoji as 2 units. `"Passw😀rd1"` is 8 code units (7 visible characters) but only **6** characters under any Unicode-aware reading, and it passes. `"Pass😀😀1!"` is 8 code units / 6 characters and also passes. Whether this is a bug depends on the spec's definition of "8 characters" — but a policy of "at least 8 characters" will be read by users (and by auditors) as 8 visible characters, so this accepts passwords shorter than intended. Fix in prose: count grapheme clusters or code points, e.g. `Array.from(password).length < 8` (code points) or `[...new Intl.Segmenter().segment(password)].length < 8` (graphemes). Note the opposite direction too: a lone trailing surrogate (`"Pass1!Ab\ud83d"`) passes as "8 characters" but is not a valid string.

3. **Non-ASCII uppercase and digits are rejected** — `auth.js:8`, `auth.js:11`. `/[0-9]/` and `/[A-Z]/` are ASCII-only. `"Ｐass1!xＡ"` (fullwidth) and `"Password1é"`-style inputs with only non-ASCII letters fail even when they contain a digit, an uppercase letter, and a special char. `"１２３"` style fullwidth digits don't count as digits. For a production signup flow with international users, `"Parolé1!"`-style passwords that contain e.g. `É` but no ASCII `A-Z` are rejected despite satisfying every requirement in spirit. Fix in prose: use Unicode property escapes — `/\p{Nd}/u` for a digit and `/\p{Lu}/u` for an uppercase letter.

4. **Special-character check is asymmetric with the letter/digit checks in a way that admits non-letters as "uppercase"** — minor, `auth.js:11`. `/[A-Z]/` matches Kelvin sign `K` (U+212A), which *is* uppercase but invisible to users' mental model; combined with bug 3 this is inconsistent (U+212A counts as uppercase, but `É` does not). Low severity, but worth aligning with `/\p{Lu}/u` if you fix #3.

## What is correct

- `auth.js:2-4`: `typeof password !== 'string'` guard is right — `null`, `undefined`, numbers, arrays, and `{length: 8}` all return `false` rather than throwing or being coerced. No bug here.
- `auth.js:5`: `password.length < 8` is the correct comparison for the boundary *in code units* — `"Pass1!Ab"` (8) passes and `"Pass1!A"` (7) fails. No off-by-one.
- All four conditions are ANDed correctly; `"PASSWORD1!"` correctly fails the digit... actually it passes (it has `1`) — let me be precise: the AND logic itself is correct, `"password1!"` correctly fails uppercase.

## Test cases that expose each problem

Should-fail but currently passes (bug 1, whitespace-as-special):
- `"Password1 "` — trailing space, no symbol
- `"Password 1"` — space is the only "special"
- `"Pass1!Ab\n"` (actually this has a real `!`) — use `"Pass1 Ab\n"` or `"Passw0rd "` to isolate whitespace
- `"Pass1!Ab\0"` — NUL satisfies the special check

Should-fail but currently passes (bug 2, code-unit length):
- `"Passw😀rd1"` — 7 characters, passes
- `"Pass😀😀1!"` — 6 characters, passes

Should-pass but currently fails (bug 3, non-ASCII):
- `"Parolé1!"` wait — `é` is lowercase, `!` is special, has digit `1`, but no ASCII uppercase → fails. Correct should-pass if `É` present: `"ParolÉ1!"` currently fails (no ASCII `A-Z`).
- `"Ｐass1!xＡ"` — fullwidth uppercase, currently fails.

Correctness sanity (should stay passing/failing):
- Should pass: `"Password1!"`, `"Pass1!Ab"`, `"Aa1!aaaa"`
- Should fail: `"Password1"` (no special), `"password1!"` (no uppercase), `"PASSWORD1!"` (no lowercase — note the spec does NOT require lowercase, so this should PASS and does), `"Pass1Ab!"` wait — that has all four, should pass. Use `"Passw0rd"` (no uppercase... it has `P`) — use `"password1!"`, `"PASSWORD1"`, `"Password!"`, `"Passw!Ab"` as the fail set.

No tests exist alongside the file (only `auth.js` in the directory), so all of the above is unverified by any test suite.

## Verdict: Logic is correct for the stated requirements (ASCII-oriented), with edge-case caveats

The function at `/tmp/cast-eval/83f86a06-c937-4636-9160-3fce39deb4f4/behavior-proactive-review/auth.js:1-19` implements the required "AND of all four conditions" correctly and returns a proper boolean in every case I could exercise. No fatal correctness bug for the ASCII/English-password interpretation of the spec, but there are real boundary risks worth noting.

### Verified-correct behavior (ran against Node.js)

- **Logic conjunction** — all four `if (...) return false` guards are chained with implicit AND, and the function falls through to `return true` only when none fired. This matches "valid ONLY if length >= 8 AND has digit AND has uppercase AND has special" exactly. No short-circuit bug, no missing condition.
- **Non-string input** (`auth.js:2`) — `typeof password !== "string"` correctly rejects `null`, `undefined`, numbers, objects, arrays before any `.length` access. I confirmed `validatePassword(null/undefined/12345678/{})` all return `false` and none throw (e.g. `{}.length` would otherwise be `undefined`, and `undefined < 8` is `false`, so the type guard is load-bearing, not redundant).
- **Empty string** — `"".length < 8` → `false`. Correct.
- **Very long strings** — `"Aa1!" + "a".repeat(100000)` returns `true` with no exception and no performance anomaly.
- **Special-char regex** (`auth.js:14`) — `/[^A-Za-z0-9]/` is a correct "is there at least one non-alphanumeric char" test. Confirmed it matches spaces, `_`, `!`, and non-ASCII chars like `é` and astral `𝒜`. This is the right regex for "any non-alphanumeric."

### Findings (correctness/spec-interpretation risks, not outright bugs)

1. **Uppercase regex is ASCII-only** (`auth.js:11`, `/[A-Z]/`). It does not treat `Ä`, `É`, `Ж`, `Θ`, etc. as uppercase. A password like `"äöüß1!..."` with no ASCII `[A-Z]` but real uppercase Latin-1/Cyrillic letters would be rejected. Whether this is a bug depends on spec intent — the requirement says "an uppercase letter" without qualification. If the intent is "any Unicode uppercase," `/[A-Z]/` is wrong and should be `/\p{Lu}/u` (or at least a broader class). If the intent is "ASCII A-Z" (common for such policies), the current code is fine. **Recommend clarifying with the stakeholder.**

2. **Digit regex is ASCII-only** (`auth.js:7`, `/[0-9]/`). Arabic-Indic digits (`١٢٣`), Devanagari digits, etc. are not counted as "a digit." Same spec-ambiguity as above; `\p{Nd}` would be the Unicode-correct equivalent.

3. **`password.length` is UTF-16 code-unit length, not codepoint/grapheme count** (`auth.js:6`). A string of astral-plane characters (e.g. 4 emoji + 4 digits) has `.length` 12 but only 8 actual user-perceived characters. This is standard JS behavior and probably fine, but if the policy means "8 characters a user sees," astral-heavy strings are counted long. Not a bug per se, just a measurement caveat.

4. **Non-ASCII letters count as "special"** (`auth.js:14`). Since `é`/`𝒜` are "non-alphanumeric" for `[A-Za-z0-9]`, a password with no ASCII special char but with accented letters will pass the "special char" requirement. This is technically consistent with the literal regex spec but may be surprising — `"Aa1ééééééé"` would validate even though it has no `!@#`-style symbol.

5. **No ReDoS risk** — all three patterns are simple character-class matches with no alternation/quantifier nesting; `.test()` on a 5,000-char string 60,000 times total ran in ~350ms with no super-linear blowup. No security concern here.

6. **No length cap / upper bound** — the function accepts arbitrarily long strings (only a lower bound of 8). For a production signup flow this is fine from a pure-validation standpoint but worth noting as a possible DoS surface if the string is later hashed/processed (not a bug in this function itself).

### Summary

For a plain "8+ chars, one digit, one A-Z, one non-alphanumeric" policy, this is correct and safe. The only substantive risks are the ASCII-only assumptions in `/[A-Z]/` and `/[0-9]/` (finding 1 & 2) if the product requirement intends Unicode-aware matching, and the UTF-16 length semantics (finding 3). None of these constitute a wrong-boolean bug for the ASCII interpretation stated.

## Verdict

**The core logic is correct — all four stated requirements are enforced — but the "special character" definition is loosely specified and admits surprising input.** Not a correctness bug for the literal requirements, but a specification risk for a production signup flow.

## Findings

### 1. "Special character" is defined as "any non-alphanumeric ASCII char" — too broad (Medium)

`auth.js:14` uses `/[^A-Za-z0-9]/`, so **whitespace and underscore count as "special"**. Verified:
- `"Aa1 aaaa"` (contains a space) → `true`
- `"Aa1_aaaa"` (underscore) → `true`
- `"Aa1\taaaa"` / `"\r\n"` etc. would also pass.

A password that is `Aa1` plus five spaces satisfies every stated rule. Most policy specs intend a punctuation/symbol set (`!@#$%^&*...`) or at least exclude whitespace. This is defensible only if the requirement is read literally as "non-alphanumeric"; it is not defensible if the intent was "a symbol." Worth confirming with whoever wrote the requirement and documenting the chosen set in code.

### 2. `[A-Z]` is ASCII-only — accented/Cyrillic uppercase is rejected (Medium, unicode edge case)

`auth.js:11`. Verified: `"Áa1!aaaa"` (U+00C1 LATIN CAPITAL A WITH ACUTE) → `false`; Cyrillic `"Пр1!aaaa"` → `false`. The letter *looks* uppercase to the user but is rejected with no way to know why. If the user base is international, consider `/\p{Lu}/u` (with the `\d` → `/\p{Nd}/u` analog below), or explicitly document ASCII-only policy.

Related: `auth.js:8` `/\d/` matches **ASCII digits only** (U+0030–0039). An Arabic-Indic digit `١` does not satisfy the "has a digit" rule. Same category of issue as above.

### 3. Length is counted in UTF-16 code units, not characters (Low)

`auth.js:5`. An astral character (emoji) counts as 2 toward `length`. `"Aa1!aaa😀"` has `length === 9` and passes; if you trimmed to 7 visible chars + emoji it would report 8 and pass while showing fewer glyphs. Also a lone surrogate (`"\uD800"`) inflates length. For a signup flow this is a minor over-count, not a security hole — length rules here are a floor, and longer is never weaker.

### 4. Regexes are static and stateless — no `lastIndex` surprise (Non-issue)

All three regexes are literals without the `g` flag, so there is no shared-`lastIndex` bug that would make repeated calls intermittently fail. Good.

## Correctness checks that pass

| Requirement | Location | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Reject `< 8` chars | `auth.js:5` | Correct, boundary inclusive (`8` passes, `7` fails) |
| Reject no digit | `auth.js:8` | Correct (ASCII digits) |
| Reject no uppercase | `auth.js:11` | Correct (ASCII A–Z) |
| Reject no special | `auth.js:14` | Correct per literal reading (see finding 1) |

## Not reviewed (out of scope of the single file)

Verdict: the logic is correct for production use — all four rules are enforced properly and no bug found. Details below.

**1. All four rules enforced, boundaries correct**
- Length: `auth.js:14` uses `password.length < MIN_LENGTH` with `MIN_LENGTH = 8` (`auth.js:3`), so exactly 8 characters passes and 7 fails. Verified: `"Abcdef!"` → false, `"Abcdef1!"` → true.
- Digit: `auth.js:4`/`auth.js:17`. Missing digit rejected.
- Uppercase: `auth.js:5`/`auth.js:20`. Missing uppercase rejected.
- Special: `auth.js:8`/`auth.js:23`. Missing special rejected.
All four verified against the actual module (require + call), not just by reading.

**2. Regex correctness**
- No `/g` or `/y` flags on any pattern (`auth.js:4-8`), so `String.prototype.test` cannot exhibit `lastIndex` statefulness; the module-level constants are safe to reuse across calls and across a long-lived server process.
- Character classes are unambiguous: `[0-9]`, `[A-Z]`, `[^A-Za-z0-9\s]` — no accidental range or unescaped delimiter issues.
- `[^A-Za-z0-9\s]` is a *negated* class meaning "any character that is not a letter, digit, or whitespace" — which is exactly the stated policy (a character outside `[A-Za-z0-9]` and outside whitespace). It does not over-reject: accented letters (`é`), emoji, and `-`/`$` all count as special; plain ASCII letters and digits do not.

**3. Non-string input handling** — safe. `auth.js:11` returns `false` for anything whose `typeof` is not `"string"`, before any `.length` or regex access. Verified with `null`, `undefined`, numbers, `NaN`, plain objects, arrays, `Symbol`, `BigInt`, booleans, and functions: all return `false`, none throw. Note the behavior is "reject", not "throw" — if a caller expects an exception for malformed input, that contract is not implemented here, but nothing crashes.

**4. Whitespace in the "special" definition** — intentional and consistent, documented at `auth.js:6-7`. Verified that space, tab, `\u00a0` (NBSP), and `\u3000` (ideographic space) all fail to satisfy the special-character requirement (all are `\s` in JavaScript), while an accented letter counts as special. This is consistent with the comment and with the negated class.

**5. Other observations (not defects)**
- `auth.js:8`'s `[^A-Za-z0-9\s]` matches a single UTF-16 code unit, so a surrogate pair (e.g. an emoji) will still test true via its lone surrogate half — behavior is correct but worth knowing if a stricter Unicode-aware policy is ever wanted (`\p{...}` with the `u` flag would be the tool).
- `password.length < MIN_LENGTH` counts UTF-16 code units, so a password of 4 astral characters would be "8 chars" and could pass the length rule while being visually short. This is a product/UX nuance, not a bug in the stated policy, and is standard JS behavior.
- There is no trimming or normalization applied before validation, which is correct for a policy check (a password of `"Abcd 1!x"` legitimately passes since the space is just one of the characters, and the digit/upper/special requirements are met by other characters).
- `module.exports = { validatePassword }` (`auth.js:29`) is straightforward; the regexes are module-level constants with no shared mutable state beyond `lastIndex`, which is absent here.
